info.title: ghosthand daemon API
info.description:
Control iPhones connected to a Mac. Screenshots come over USB (QuickTime
screen capture). Taps, swipes and keys go through a Bluetooth HID mouse and
keyboard that the Mac serves; the iPhone shows it as an AssistiveTouch pointer.

## Transport

The daemon always listens on a unix socket, `~/.ghosthand/daemon.sock`:

    curl --unix-socket ~/.ghosthand/daemon.sock http://localhost/v1/devices

The unix socket needs no token: its file permissions allow only the owner.

From another computer, call the same routes through the Mac's tunnel. The daemon keeps a
connection to ghosthand.dev while the Mac is signed in, so it needs no open port:

    ghosthand tunnel url --new-token            # on the Mac: prints export lines for GHOSTHAND_URL and GHOSTHAND_TOKEN
    # on the other computer, after pasting them:
    curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $GHOSTHAND_TOKEN" $GHOSTHAND_URL/v1/devices

The URL is `https://ghosthand.dev/macs/<mac>` and the token is an API token of the
account. `GET https://ghosthand.dev/macs` lists the Macs. Through the tunnel a request
body is at most 20 MB, and only the routes under `/v1/` are served.

On a Mac signed in to the account, the unix socket also reaches the other Macs:
`GET /v1/devices` lists their iPhones too (each with its `mac`), `POST /v1/leases` with
such a `device` takes it on its Mac and returns a lease like `studio:42`, and every
route under `/v1/leases/studio:42/` goes to that Mac through ghosthand.dev.

The CLI sends `User-Agent: ghosthand-cli/<version>`. When npm has a newer ghosthand,
unix socket responses to it carry `ghosthand-latest-version: <version>`, and the CLI
prints an update notice.

## Coordinates

`x` and `y` are pixels of the image from `GET /v1/leases/{lease}/screenshot`.

## Long requests and progress

Input operations (tap, swipe, scroll, key, type) can wait up to 300 s while the
iPhone pairs over Bluetooth. Send `Accept: text/event-stream` to get
progress as server-sent events on the same request:

    event: log
    data: {"message":"checking Bluetooth device 1A2B3C4D by moving its pointer"}

    event: result
    data: {"message":"tapped 414,896","logs":[...]}

A failure ends the stream with `event: error` and a `Problem` as data.
In stream mode the HTTP status is always 200; read the last event.
The stream also carries `: ping` comment lines every second. When the
client disconnects, the daemon stops the operation before its next
Bluetooth action. Without that header the response is one JSON body after
the operation ends, and a disconnect does not stop the operation.

Errors are always `application/problem+json`, whatever `Accept` says.

## Result of an input in the same call

Input routes take `waitText`, `screenshot` and `screentext` query parameters. They run
after the input, on the same lease, and the result carries the image and OCR text:

    POST /v1/leases/42/tap?screenshot=png&screentext=true   {"text":"General"}

An error in these steps says the input was sent; never repeat the input blindly.

## MCP

The same operations are MCP tools at `https://ghosthand.dev/mcp` (OAuth with the
ghosthand.dev account). It reaches every signed-in Mac of the account through its
tunnel; it is not part of this document.

## Leases

Screenshots and input run on a lease, so two agents never drive one iPhone at the
same time. `POST /v1/leases` takes an iPhone and returns the lease id; every route
under `/v1/leases/{lease}/` then runs on that iPhone:

    curl --unix-socket ~/.ghosthand/daemon.sock -H 'content-type: application/json' \
      -d '{"device":"default","reason":"reply to Anna in Messages"}' \
      http://localhost/v1/leases                                  # {"id":"studio:42",...}
    curl --unix-socket ~/.ghosthand/daemon.sock http://localhost/v1/leases/42/text

A lease ends by itself after `idleTimeoutSeconds` (default 600) without a call.
IDs increase in state.db, including across daemon restarts, expiry and release.
`label` is only display text, not a way to resume a lease. Lease IDs are not remote
authentication: the tunnel requires an API token. A lease carries the slug of the Mac
that holds it, e.g. `studio:42`, so it works from every Mac of the account; only a Mac
that is signed out returns `42`. The plain `42` also works on the Mac that holds it.

Acquiring a lease turns AssistiveTouch on when it is off. Releasing the lease (or its
expiry) turns it off again, only when ghosthand turned it on.

## XCTest mode

An iPhone can use XCTest instead of Bluetooth (`PUT /v1/leases/{lease}/control`). Then
input and screenshots go through WebDriverAgent, an XCUITest runner the daemon builds
and starts with Xcode. The routes stay the same; the few that XCTest cannot do fail
with `unsupported-in-mode`. Recording and previews still use USB screen capture.

servers.description: The Mac's tunnel, from any computer. Needs an API token from `ghosthand tunnel url --new-token`.

mac.description: The Mac's slug, from `ghosthand tunnel url` or `GET https://ghosthand.dev/macs`

servers.description: Unix socket `~/.ghosthand/daemon.sock` (`curl --unix-socket`; the host part is ignored). No token.

get.description:
iPhones that USB screen capture shows, with their model, lock state, Bluetooth link
and lease. Waits up to 25 s for a trusted USB iPhone to appear after a daemon start;
fails in about 0.1 s when USB has no trusted iPhone. With none, returns a `no-device`
problem that says what USB lockdown sees (not on USB, not trusted, locked).
On the unix socket of a signed-in Mac, the list also has the iPhones of the account's
other online Macs (`mac` says where); a Mac that cannot answer adds a warning.

metadata.title: List connected iPhones

get.description:
For the ghosthand app (setup window and control plane). Unlike `/v1/devices` it answers
at once, from USB lockdown, and also lists iPhones that screen capture does not show yet:
not trusted, or locked. Each iPhone has one `step`, the next thing a person must do
(`ready` when agents can use it), so a client needs no logic of its own. `phones` is
sorted by `id`, so the order is stable. `macName` is the name the iPhone lists under
Settings > Bluetooth.

metadata.title: List iPhones with their setup step

get.description:
A small read-only JPEG of the screen, for the control plane: it shows what an agent is
doing. It needs no lease and does not touch one (no idle reset, no `lastCommand`). It
opens USB screen capture like a screenshot does, but never requests Camera permission.
Missing access needs the setup app's Allow Camera button. A locked iPhone fails at once with `device-locked`. Without a frame it can
wait up to about 10 s. With capture running it returns the newest frame at once, so the
control plane polls it at 30 fps; the capture stays open 60 s after the last call.

metadata.title: Preview a screen without a lease

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: `id` (USB UDID) from `GET /v1/phones`.

parameters.name: width
parameters.description: Image width in pixels; the height keeps the screen's aspect ratio.

put.description:
For the setup app only, after a user click. Saves the mode and, for `xctest`, builds
and starts WebDriverAgent in the background; `GET /v1/phones` shows its progress in
`xctest`. Fails with `device-leased` while an agent holds the iPhone. Agents use
`PUT /v1/leases/{lease}/control` instead.

parameters.name: phone
parameters.description: `id` (USB UDID) from `GET /v1/phones`.

202.description: Saved; the runner starts in the background

post.summary: Press key from the control plane
post.description:
For the control plane's Take Control only: a person presses a key on the iPhone. No lease:
it works also while an agent holds the iPhone, between the agent's commands, and does
not touch that lease. Only on the unix socket. Agents use `POST /v1/leases/{lease}/key`.

post.summary: Type text from the control plane
post.description:
For the control plane's Take Control only: a person types text on the iPhone. No lease, like
`POST /v1/phones/{phone}/key`. Only on the unix socket. Agents use `POST /v1/leases/{lease}/type`.

For the control plane's Take Control only: a person clicks the live screen and the iPhone
gets a tap there. `x` and `y` are fractions of the screen (0...1), so the app needs no
screen size. No lease, like `POST /v1/phones/{phone}/key`. In Bluetooth mode it turns
AssistiveTouch on when off; `POST /v1/phones/{phone}/release` turns it off again if no
lease holds the iPhone, else it goes off 60 s after the person's last input. Only on the unix socket. Agents use `POST /v1/leases/{lease}/tap`.

For the control plane's Take Control only: a person drags on the live screen and the
iPhone gets a swipe with the same start, end and duration. Like `POST /v1/leases/{lease}/swipe`
it is a human-like flick, lifted while still moving. No lease, and AssistiveTouch like
`POST /v1/phones/{phone}/tap`. Only on the unix socket.

post.summary: Release control from the control plane
post.description:
For the control plane's Release Control: the person stops tapping and typing. AssistiveTouch
that a tap or swipe turned on goes off at once if no lease holds the iPhone. Without this
call it goes off 60 s after the last input. Only on the unix socket.

Returns a new lease id for the routes under `/v1/leases/{lease}/`. Fails at once
with `device-leased` while another lease holds the iPhone. The problem detail
shows its label, reason, when it was acquired and when it was last used, so the
client can decide to give up instead of retrying. `force` ends that lease
instead (after its running operation); its next call gets `lease-invalid`.
`waitSeconds` waits for the other lease to end instead. Send
`Accept: text/event-stream` with it, so a closed connection stops the wait
(events `log`, then `result` with the Lease, or `error`).
On the unix socket, a `device` that is on another Mac of the account (or the only
iPhone of the account, when this Mac has none) is taken on that Mac; the id is then
`<mac>:<number>`.
Every acquire asks ghosthand.dev if the plan covers this iPhone on this Mac (free:
one iPhone; Pro: every iPhone on each paid Mac). Not covered: `subscription-required`
with the subscribe and dashboard links. ghosthand.dev unreachable: only an iPhone
allowed in a recent check is leased; any other gets `tunnel-offline`.

metadata.title: Take exclusive use of one iPhone

x-codeSamples.label: CLI
x-codeSamples.source: ghosthand acquire --label ses_123 --reason "reply to Anna in Messages"

x-codeSamples.label: Socket
x-codeSamples.source:
curl --unix-socket ~/.ghosthand/daemon.sock http://localhost/v1/leases \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"device":"default","label":"ses_123","reason":"reply to Anna in Messages"}'

201.description: Lease taken. JSON by default, server-sent events with `Accept text/event-stream`.

delete.description:
Waits for a running operation of the lease, then frees the iPhone for the next `POST /v1/leases`.
Turns AssistiveTouch off, also when it was on before the lease, unless `keepAssistiveTouch`.
A lease that ends by its idle timeout turns it off too, a few seconds later.

metadata.title: End a lease and free the iPhone

parameters.name: keepAssistiveTouch
parameters.description: Leave AssistiveTouch on after the release.

get.description:
The current screen as PNG or JPEG, in about 0.3 s. The capture stops 1 s after the
last frame to save CPU, and restarting it adds about 0.2 s. The image is in screen points by default (see
`scale`): its pixels are the coordinates that `tap`, `swipe` and `scroll` take.

metadata.title: Take a screenshot of the iPhone screen

parameters.name: settle
parameters.description: Wait until two frames 150 ms apart match (up to 2 s), so an animation after an action is finished.

parameters.name: native
parameters.description:
Take a real iOS screenshot instead (cmd+shift+3 on the Bluetooth keyboard), read it
over USB, then delete it from Photos. About 2 s. It shows system dialogs that USB
screen capture leaves out. The iPhone must be unlocked and paired over Bluetooth.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: Image format of the response body.

X-Note.description: With `native`, what happened to the screenshot file on the iPhone (deleted, or kept and why)

get.description:
On-device text recognition (Vision, accurate level, English plus an optional language) of a
fresh frame. Boxes use a top-left origin in the same space as the screenshot
and `tap` (screen points by default, see `scale`). About 0.1 s for the frame
plus 0.05-0.25 s for OCR.

metadata.title: Read the text on screen with OCR

parameters.name: settle
parameters.description: Wait until two frames 150 ms apart match (up to 2 s) before OCR.

200.description: Recognized text lines, top to bottom

post.description:
Tap at a point with a 220...260 ms press, or at text found by OCR. With `text`, OCR reads the screen (native
pixels, `language`) and taps the center of the matching line: a line equal to `text`
(case-insensitive) wins over lines that only contain it. Several matches fail with a
numbered list, top to bottom; pick one with `index`.

metadata.title: Tap at a point or on text

x-codeSamples.label: CLI
x-codeSamples.source:
ghosthand tap -l 42 207 448 --screenshot after.png
ghosthand tap -l 42 --text General --wait-text About

post.description:
Two mouse clicks at one point, with 220...260 ms presses and a 100...150 ms
release-to-press gap. Select a word or zoom supported content. App behavior
varies; this is not a VoiceOver gesture or a side-button confirmation.
With text, resolve the matching OCR line once before both clicks.

Three mouse clicks at one point, timed like `double-tap`. Selects a paragraph or
line in text views that support it. With text, resolve the OCR line once before the clicks.

Press and hold at a point, or at text found by OCR (like `tap`), for `durationMs`
without moving, then release. A long press: context menus, Home Screen icon menus,
link previews. No reports are sent while held: iOS reads repeated reports as movement.

metadata.title: Press and hold (long press)

x-codeSamples.label: CLI
x-codeSamples.source:
ghosthand hold -l 42 60 120 --screenshot after.png
ghosthand hold -l 42 --text Safari --duration 1500

post.description:
A quick human-like finger swipe from `from` to `to`: fast start, lifted while still
moving, so feeds like TikTok and lists keep going. Speed, easing and a slight sideways
bow are random on every call; `durationMs` fixes the speed. Use it for Home Screen
pages, feeds, carousels, pickers and sliders. For exact drag and drop use `hold-drag`.

metadata.title: Swipe like a finger

post.description:
Press at `from`, stay still for `holdMs` (a long press), then drag to `to` with the
button still held and release. Moves items that start dragging after a long press,
like Home Screen icons. From the normal Home Screen, icons need `holdMs` 2500
(iOS enters edit mode while held).

metadata.title: Long press, then drag

post.description:
Moves the pointer to `at` (default: screen center), then sends wheel ticks there.
Scrolls lists that a drag cannot scroll (a drag on a UITableView row is a tap).

metadata.title: Scroll with the mouse wheel

post.description:
Press a key, a key combination or a media key on the Bluetooth keyboard. `home` goes
to the Home Screen. For mute use `POST /v1/leases/{lease}/mute`: the Mute key is a
toggle and `key` refuses it.

metadata.title: Press a key or key combination

x-codeSamples.label: CLI
x-codeSamples.source:
ghosthand key -l 42 home --screenshot s.png
ghosthand key -l 42 cmd+space

post.description:
Types US-ASCII text on the Bluetooth keyboard into the focused field. Tap the field
first. For secrets, send the text in the body only; it is not logged.

metadata.title: Type text with the Bluetooth keyboard

post.description:
Do a task in plain words ("open the TikTok likes tab") on the lease's iPhone. An agent on
ghosthand.dev (a fast model, Claude Haiku 5.5) reads the screen with OCR and sends
the taps, swipes and keys through this Mac's tunnel, then answers in one or two
sentences. One call is one turn; the task keeps its history, so `task` sends a
follow-up to the same task. A follow-up while a turn runs stops that turn first. The task ends one day after its last turn. The agent gets
the iPhone's name, model, iOS version, language and region (as `info` reads them).

With `Accept: text/event-stream` the response is the turn's AI SDK UI message stream,
unchanged: `data: <chunk JSON>` events (`start`, `tool-input-available`,
`tool-output-available`, `text-delta`, `finish`, ...), then `data: [DONE]`. A failure
is an `error` chunk. Closing the stream stops the task. Without that header the
response is one JSON body after the turn ends.

Needs a signed-in Mac with its tunnel connected. The task uses the lease; do not send
other input to the iPhone while it runs.

x-codeSamples.label: CLI
x-codeSamples.source:
ghosthand task -l 42 "open Settings > General > About and tell me the iOS version"
ghosthand task -l 42 --resume tsk_8f2k3x "now go back to the Home Screen"

x-codeSamples.label: Socket
x-codeSamples.source:
curl -N --unix-socket ~/.ghosthand/daemon.sock http://localhost/v1/leases/42/task \
  -H 'accept: text/event-stream' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"open the TikTok likes tab"}'

Ghosthand-Task.description: The task id; pass it as `task` to send a follow-up

schema.description: AI SDK UI message stream: `data: <UIMessageChunk>` events, then `data: [DONE]`

post.description:
Presses the Bluetooth keyboard Mute key (consumer 0xE2), which toggles iOS full
mute: all output, media in every app too. The ringer switch is separate. Each press
is confirmed by SpringBoard's system log line over USB. If the first press toggled
the wrong way (the iPhone was already in the asked state), it presses once more.
Without a confirmation it fails with `mute-unconfirmed` and never presses again.

metadata.title: Mute or unmute all iPhone sound

post.description: Clicks at the top center (the status bar), then waits for a USB frame. Needs a paired iPhone. A locked iPhone fails with `device-locked`; `unlock` also wakes it.

metadata.title: Turn the display on with a Bluetooth click

post.description:
Bluetooth keyboard only: Enter wakes the screen, Enter opens the passcode screen,
then the passcode is typed once (about 3 s). Locked-screen USB capture is unavailable, so the screen cannot be checked.
Success is checked with the lock state over USB. A wrong passcode is not retried (`unlock-failed`),
because failed tries count toward the iPhone lockout. An unlocked iPhone
is left as it is. The passcode is not stored.

metadata.title: Wake a locked iPhone and type its passcode

post.description: Sends Control-Command-Q through the paired keyboard, then checks the lock state over USB (`lock-failed` when it did not lock).

metadata.title: Lock the iPhone over Bluetooth

post.description:
Records the iPhone screen (H.264) and its sound (AAC) from the same USB capture as
screenshots, so screenshots and input keep working while it records. The file is
written on the daemon's Mac. It stops by itself after `maxDurationSeconds`, when the
lease ends (release, idle timeout, `force`), or when the daemon stops; the file is
complete in each case. One recording per iPhone at a time (`recording-active`).
A locked iPhone fails with `device-locked`.

metadata.title: Start a screen recording to a video file

post.description:
Returns when the file is complete. After an automatic stop (max duration) it returns
that recording's result once. `no-recording` when nothing was recorded since the last
stop. `recording-failed` when the video writer failed (for example a full disk).

metadata.title: Stop the screen recording and finish the file

get.description: Read over USB lockdown in about 35 ms, also while the iPhone is locked.

metadata.title: Read whether AssistiveTouch is on

put.description:
Writes the setting over USB lockdown (about 40 ms, also while locked), with no
touch on the iPhone. Without AssistiveTouch the iPhone shows no pointer and drops
clicks, so acquire, tap, swipe and wake turn it on by themselves. Release
turns it off again when ghosthand turned it on; the Bluetooth link stays connected.

metadata.title: Turn AssistiveTouch on or off over USB

get.description: How the daemon sends input to the iPhone (Bluetooth or XCTest), and the XCTest runner state.

metadata.title: Read whether input goes over Bluetooth or XCTest

put.description:
`xctest` builds WebDriverAgent for this iPhone when needed (1-3 min the first time),
starts it and waits until it answers; calling it again restarts the runner. Needs
Xcode signed in to an Apple account, Developer Mode, the developer trusted on the
iPhone and UI Automation on; errors say which step is missing. `bluetooth` stops the
runner. Stream with `Accept: text/event-stream` to see the build steps.

metadata.title: Switch input between Bluetooth and XCTest

put.description:
Writes the name over USB lockdown (Settings > General > About > Name), with no
touch on the iPhone. Screen capture keeps the old name until the cable is plugged
in again; the device id does not change.

metadata.title: Rename the iPhone over USB

delete.description:
Removes this Mac's Bluetooth bond with the iPhone. The fix when pairing fails because
one side kept an old bond. Also forget the Mac on the iPhone, then pair again from its
Settings > Bluetooth. Clears the saved pointer mode too.

metadata.title: Remove the Mac's Bluetooth bond with the iPhone

get.description:
Lists a folder on the iPhone over USB (AFC). Without `app` the root is the media
folder, /var/mobile/Media: DCIM (Camera Roll files), Downloads, Books, PublicStaging.
With `app` the root is that app's Documents, only for apps with file sharing
(`fileSharing` in `GET apps`). Works while the iPhone is locked, after its first
unlock since boot. No Developer Mode.

metadata.title: List files on the iPhone over USB

parameters.name: recursive
parameters.description: Also list everything in subfolders. Folders iOS does not allow are skipped.

200.description: Entries of the folder; a file path gives that one file

delete.description:
Removes a file, or a folder with everything in it. Refuses /DCIM: a Camera Roll file
removed over AFC stays as a broken photo in Photos; use `POST photos/delete`.

metadata.title: Remove a file on the iPhone over USB

get.description:
The bytes of an iPhone file. A folder comes as a zip of the folder
(`Content-Type: application/zip`).

metadata.title: Copy a file from the iPhone over USB

X-File-Name.description: Name of the file, or of the folder with `.zip` added

put.description:
Writes the request body to a file on the iPhone, replacing it, and makes missing
folders. Files in the media folder are not in any app: a photo copied to /DCIM does
not appear in Photos (see the README for ways to add photos).

metadata.title: Copy a file to the iPhone over USB

post.description:
Uploads the request body to ghosthand.dev with this Mac's account and returns a
short link that lasts 1 day. Open it in Safari on the iPhone and tap Save: the share
sheet then offers Save Video or Save Image, which adds the file to Photos. No lease:
nothing runs on the iPhone. At most 100 MB.

metadata.title: Upload a file for the iPhone to save to Photos

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: File name with its extension; Photos needs the extension to know the type, e.g. clip.mp4

get.description: Camera Roll files (photos, videos, screenshots) under /DCIM, newest first.

metadata.title: List the newest photos on the iPhone

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Newest files to return, 1-10000

post.description:
Deletes Camera Roll files by name through ImageCaptureCore, like Image Capture.app,
so the Photos library forgets them too. Permanent: they skip Recently Deleted. The
iPhone must be unlocked.

metadata.title: Delete photos from the iPhone library

get.description:
Installed apps over USB (installation_proxy), with their Home Screen place
(springboardservices). `installing` marks App Store downloads that are not done yet.

metadata.title: List the apps on the iPhone

parameters.name: system
parameters.description: Also list Apple's built-in apps

200.description: Apps, user apps first, by name

post.description:
Installs the .ipa in the request body. iOS checks the signature: only IPAs signed
for this iPhone install (ad hoc, enterprise, or development with this iPhone in the
profile). App Store apps come from the App Store app.

metadata.title: Install an IPA on the iPhone

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: File name of the IPA, for messages

delete.description: Removes the app and its data, like Remove App > Delete App on the iPhone.

metadata.title: Uninstall an app from the iPhone

parameters.name: bundle
parameters.description: Bundle id from `GET apps`, e.g. com.burbn.instagram

get.description: Model, iOS build, serial number, battery, storage, language and time zone over USB lockdown. Works while locked.

metadata.title: Read battery, storage and iOS version

get.description:
Lines of the iPhone system log (syslog_relay) during the next `seconds`. iOS keeps
no history for this stream: start it, then do what you want to watch.

metadata.title: Read the iPhone system log

parameters.name: seconds
parameters.description: How long to read, 1-120

parameters.name: grep
parameters.description: Keep lines that contain this (case-insensitive)

parameters.name: process
parameters.description: Keep lines of this process, e.g. SpringBoard or appstored

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Stop after this many lines, 1-10000

post.description:
Restarts or shuts down the iPhone over USB (diagnostics_relay). After a restart iOS
ignores the Bluetooth keyboard until a person types the passcode once.

metadata.title: Restart or shut down the iPhone

post.description:
Makes a random name, last name, username, 18+ birthdate or password for a new account,
and saves it in state.db with the lease's reason, label and iPhone. `username` is built
from the newest name and last name made on this lease, else from random ones. Values
are never deleted: `GET /v1/random` lists them after the lease ends.

metadata.title: Make and save a random account detail

get.description: Every saved random value, newest first. Needs no lease, so values stay readable after their lease ends.

metadata.title: List saved random account details

parameters.name: lease
parameters.description: Only the values made on this lease

get.description:
Poll every 2 seconds after opening setup. Works before permissions, USB trust or
Bluetooth pairing are complete. Never requests permissions, opens windows, sends
input or acquires a lease. Continue when ready is true. If several phones are
connected, select the intended phone with device; do not use another ready phone.

parameters.name: device
parameters.description: USB id, capture id or exact phone name. Omit only for a single phone.

200.description: Current readiness and setup steps, including incomplete setup

post.description: The Mac shows under Settings > Bluetooth on the iPhone for 30 s. Call again to extend; it stops by itself when calls stop. Call it only while a phone's `step` is `pair`.

metadata.title: Make the Mac discoverable for Bluetooth pairing

post.description:
Called by the setup app only after a user clicks an Allow button. Normal commands
never request permissions. Agents run `ghosthand setup` once, then poll setup status
until ready while the user follows the app. Already allowed or denied permissions do not show another prompt;
denied permissions need the setup app's Open Settings button.

202.description: Permission request started; read GET /v1/phones for its result

get.description:
The Mac's sign-in state and, when signed in, the plan from ghosthand.dev (one
request to the server). Every lease needs a signed-in account: free covers one
iPhone, Pro covers every iPhone on each paid Mac. `GET /v1/phones` carries the same
sign-in state without the plan and without a server request.

post.description:
Creates an API token for scripts that call this API from another computer through
`https://ghosthand.dev/macs/<mac>`. The token works for every Mac of the account and
is shown once. Unix socket only: a token must not be able to create more tokens.

post.description:
Starts a browser sign-in (OAuth device flow) and returns `verificationUrl` to open.
The daemon polls ghosthand.dev by itself until the user approves, denies, or the
link expires; read the result from `GET /v1/phones` or `GET /v1/account`. Calling it
again while a sign-in runs returns the same link. Unix socket only: the setup app
and `ghosthand account login` call it, agents do not.

metadata.title: Stop the daemon

post.description:
The daemon stops like `POST /v1/daemon/stop`, then runs the binary on disk
again (or `executable`) with the same arguments and environment. Use it after
a rebuild or an update. The pid stays the same; `startedAt` changes.
Leases live in state.db and stay valid.

metadata.title: Restart the daemon with the same arguments

post.summary: Update now, or turn auto-update on or off
post.description:
Without a body: reads the latest release from ghosthand.dev now and installs it in
~/Applications/Ghosthand.app when it is a newer build, even with auto-update off. It
installs only while no lease is active, and the daemon restarts on it once idle.
With `auto`: only saves the setting. Only over the unix socket; tunnel clients get 403.

get.description: The OpenAPI document the daemon was built from, so a client can check the exact routes it serves.

metadata.title: Download this OpenAPI document

200.description: The spec the daemon was built from

bearerAuth.description: Required on the tunnel. An API token of the account, from `ghosthand tunnel url --new-token`. The unix socket needs no token

Scale.name: scale
Scale.description:
Coordinate space of images and points, as a fraction of the native screen pixels.
Default: screen points (1/2 on @2x iPhones, 1/3 on @3x), e.g. 414x896 on an iPhone XR
instead of 828x1792. Points keep UI text readable for vision models at about a third
of the tokens, and stay under every model's resize limit, so coordinates the model
reads from the image are the ones to send. Use 1 for native pixels.

Language.name: language
Language.description: OCR language, a BCP 47 tag (e.g. it-IT). English en-US is always included.

WaitText.name: waitText
WaitText.description:
After the input, read the screen with OCR every 150 ms until a line contains this
text (case-insensitive). On timeout it fails with `wait-text-timeout`: the input was
sent and is never repeated.

TimeoutMs.name: timeoutMs
TimeoutMs.description: Deadline of `waitText`, counted from the end of the input. Needs `waitText`.

Screenshot.name: screenshot
Screenshot.description:
After the input (and `waitText`), wait until the screen is still, then return its image
in `screenshot` of the result, in the `scale` space.

Screentext.name: screentext
Screentext.description:
After the input (and `waitText`), wait until the screen is still, then return its OCR
text in `screen` of the result. OCR runs on the native frame, boxes are in the `scale`
space. With `screenshot`, both come from the same frame.

FileApp.name: app
FileApp.description: Bundle id of an app with file sharing; the path is then inside its container, e.g. /Documents/a.pdf

Lease.name: lease
Lease.description: Lease id from `POST /v1/leases`. Unknown, expired, released or taken with `force` gives `lease-invalid`.

Action.description: Input sent. JSON by default, server-sent events with `Accept text/event-stream`.

Problem.description: Error (RFC 9457 problem details). `code` is stable; switch on it, not on `title` or `detail`.

example.title: iPhone leased by another client
example.detail:
Tommy's iPhone is in use by another lease:
  ses_456 (book a table on OpenTable), acquired 2 min ago, last used 10 s ago (tap)
Decide first: if that task is still active, give up or tell the user the iPhone is busy.

LeaseId.description:
Lease id: the slug of the Mac that holds it and a decimal number that only increases,
e.g. `studio:42` (`42` when that Mac is signed out). Pass it back exactly as returned.
Whoever has it can use the iPhone.

message.description: What the daemon did, for people and logs

url.description: Share page for Safari on the iPhone. Anyone with the link can download the file until it expires.

expiresAt.description: The link answers 404 after this, 1 day after the upload

auto.description: Turn auto-update on or off. Saved in the macOS defaults `com.remorses.ghosthand AutoUpdate`.
The daemon installs new releases by itself (default on)

latest.description: Build id of the latest release on ghosthand.dev. Absent before the first answer.

checkedAt.description: When the latest release was last asked for

message.description: The update state in one line, e.g. up to date, downloaded, installed, or why it failed

executable.description:
Absolute path of another ghosthand binary to run, e.g. a newer version the
CLI was installed as. Only over the unix socket; tunnel clients get 403.

ifIdle.description:
Restart only when no lease is active; otherwise 409 `daemon-busy` and the
daemon keeps running. macOS screen capture needs seconds to a minute after a
restart, so an agent holding a lease would lose its screen. The CLI sets it
when it restarts the daemon by itself.

version.description: Version of the daemon binary, same as the npm package

pid.description: Process id. It stays the same across `POST /v1/daemon/restart`.

executable.description: CLI binary that Ghosthand.app was installed from. Restart installs this path again, unless it gets `executable`.

safeRestart.description: Supports executable selection and ifIdle lease protection. Missing or false means the CLI must not automatically restart this daemon.

buildId.description: Changes when `executable` is rebuilt. Compare it with the CLI to find a stale daemon.

startedAt.description: When the daemon (or its last restart) started

state.description:
`not-started`: allowed, but no USB iPhone uses Bluetooth mode yet; starts on the first
Bluetooth command or when list or setup sees one. `starting`: waiting for
Bluetooth or HID publication. `on`: the HID service is published. Permission states
are checked before hardware state. Missing or denied permission tells the agent to
run setup and poll setup status until ready. Only the setup app's buttons request permissions
or open privacy settings. `powered-off`: turn Bluetooth on.
`unsupported`: authorized, but Classic is unavailable. `error`: service failure.

error.description: Why Bluetooth is not available, e.g. it is off or not allowed for the daemon

id.description: Pass it to `DELETE /v1/tunnel/tokens/{id}` to revoke the token

token.description: Send as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Shown once; store it like a password.

url.description: Base URL of this Mac through the tunnel. Absent while the Mac is not connected.

tunnel.description:
The connection to ghosthand.dev that serves remote MCP (https://ghosthand.dev/mcp)
and this API from other computers. It runs while the Mac is signed in.

connected.description: False while signed out, or while the daemon connects or reconnects

mac.description: This Mac's slug in the account, e.g. `studio`. MCP leases on it look like `studio:42`.

url.description: Base URL of this API through the tunnel, e.g. `https://ghosthand.dev/macs/studio`. Absent until connected.

warnings.description: Bluetooth problems, and capture devices that cannot be matched to a USB iPhone yet (what to do).

Control.description:
How input reaches the iPhone. `bluetooth` (default): the Mac is a Bluetooth mouse and
keyboard; screenshots come from USB screen capture. `xctest`: WebDriverAgent, an XCUITest
runner, taps, types and takes screenshots (they show dialogs that USB capture hides).
Needs Xcode, Developer Mode and UI Automation. No passcode unlock, mute or keyboard shortcuts.

XCTestRunner.description: WebDriverAgent on this iPhone. Present only in XCTest mode.

team.description: Apple team id that signs the runner, e.g. `92MF9DG2LR`

state.description:
`stopped`: not started since the daemon started; the next command starts it (about
15 s). `building`: Xcode builds it (1-3 min the first time). `starting`: launched,
waiting for its HTTP server. `running`: input works. `failed`: see `error`.

error.description: Why the last start failed and what to do

team.description: Apple team id that signs WebDriverAgent. Default the only Apple Development certificate in the keychain.

rebuild.description: Build WebDriverAgent again (e.g. after the free team's 7-day signature expired)

id.description: USB capture device id. Pass it as `device` to `POST /v1/leases`.

mac.description:
Slug of the Mac the iPhone is plugged into, e.g. `studio`. Absent while this Mac is
signed out or not connected to ghosthand.dev.

name.description: Name of the iPhone, from Settings > General > About > Name

model.description: Product type read over USB lockdown, e.g. `iPhone8,1`

modelName.description: Marketing name for `model`, e.g. `iPhone 6s`. Absent for product types ghosthand does not know yet

iosVersion.description: iOS version read over USB lockdown, e.g. `15.8.3`

phoneNumber.description: Phone number of the SIM, read over USB lockdown (`PhoneNumber`), e.g. `+39 333 123 4567`. Absent without a SIM, or when the carrier did not write the number to it.

locked.description: True while the iPhone needs its passcode, read over USB (lockdown `PasswordProtected`). Absent when unknown, e.g. two iPhones with the same name.

assistiveTouch.description: True while AssistiveTouch is on, read over USB. acquire turns it on by itself. Absent when unknown.

account.description: Sign-in state only; no plan fields and no server request

macName.description: The name this Mac shows under Settings > Bluetooth on the iPhone

camera.description:
macOS Camera permission of the daemon, needed for screen capture. Until it is
`authorized`, phones have no `captureId`. `notDetermined`: the user clicks Allow
Camera in setup. `denied`: the user opens Camera privacy settings from setup.
`restricted`: blocked by macOS policy. Commands and previews never ask by themselves.

photos.description:
Optional macOS removable volumes access, used only to delete photos on the iPhone
(`photo delete`, `screenshot --native`). The user clicks Allow Photos in setup.

remotePhones.description:
Only on the unix socket: iPhones of the account's other online Macs, each with
`mac` and `macName`, for the control plane. Each Mac pushes its list through
ghosthand.dev when it changes, so the response makes no request. Lease times
(`lastUsedAt`, `lastCommand`, `expiresAt`) can be old. Absent when there are none.

developerMode.description: Settings > Privacy & Security > Developer Mode, read over USB. XCTest mode needs it. Absent on iOS 15 and when unknown.

id.description: USB lockdown id (UDID). Not the id of `/v1/devices`; that is `captureId`.

captureId.description: Screen capture id, the one `list` prints and `acquire -d` takes. Absent until screen capture shows the iPhone and it is matched to its USB device.

modelName.description: Marketing name, e.g. `iPhone XR`. Absent for unknown product types

phoneNumber.description: Phone number of the SIM, e.g. `+39 333 123 4567`. Absent without a SIM, when the carrier did not write it, or when the iPhone is not trusted.

step.description:
The next thing a person must do, in this order:
`trust`: unlock the iPhone and tap Trust. `unlock`: trusted, needs its passcode.
`usbUnreadable`: trusted, but the lock state or Bluetooth address could not be read over USB.
Bluetooth mode: `bluetoothUnavailable`: Bluetooth is not ready on this Mac (see `bluetooth`).
`pair`: pair the Mac from iPhone Settings > Bluetooth; if the Mac is not listed,
turn Bluetooth off and on again on the iPhone. `connecting`: paired, the link
is down; the Mac reconnects.
XCTest mode: `developerMode`: turn on Developer Mode on the iPhone. `xctestStarting`:
WebDriverAgent builds or starts. `xctestFailed`: its start failed (`xctest.error`).
`ready`: agents can use it.

assistiveTouch.description: True while AssistiveTouch is on, read over USB. Absent when unknown.

waiting.description: Clients running `ghosthand wait` for this iPhone, oldest first

mac.description: Only in `remotePhones`. Slug of the Mac the iPhone is plugged into, e.g. `studio`

macName.description: Only in `remotePhones`. Name of that Mac, e.g. `Tommy's Mac Studio`

ready.description: True only when this Mac is signed in (`overview.account.state` is `signed-in`) and one selected phone has Camera access, USB capture, is unlocked and has connected Bluetooth.

next.description: The one thing the user must do next, in words an agent can pass on (the step the setup window shows), e.g. `Plug the iPhone into Tommy's Mac with a USB data cable, then unlock it.` When ready, says so.

device.description: Selected USB id. Absent if no phone matches or selection is ambiguous.

MacPermission.description: `photos`: macOS removable volumes access, so photo delete and native screenshots can delete photos (optional)

label.description: Display text the client gave, e.g. an agent session id

reason.description: The task the client waits to do

LeaseInfo.description: Who holds the iPhone. Present while a lease is active. Never has the lease id.

label.description: Display text the holder gave, e.g. an agent session id

reason.description: The task the iPhone is used for

lastUsedAt.description: The last call on the lease (or acquiredAt before the first)

lastCommand.description: CLI name of the last call on the lease, e.g. `tap` or `screenshot`. Absent before the first

expiresAt.description: When the lease ends if no call uses it before

reason.description: The task the iPhone is used for, shown to others in `GET /v1/devices` and `device-leased` errors, so they can decide to wait or give up

device.description: USB id or name from `GET /v1/devices`, or `default` when exactly one iPhone is connected

mac.description:
Slug of the Mac the iPhone is on (`mac` from `GET /v1/devices`). On the unix socket,
another Mac's slug sends the acquire straight to that Mac, without listing every Mac
first. Through the tunnel it must be this Mac's slug or omitted.

label.description: Optional display text shown to others in `GET /v1/devices` and `device-leased` errors, e.g. an agent session id. Not checked and not unique

idleTimeoutSeconds.description: The lease ends this long after its last call

force.description: End another lease on the iPhone and take it. Only for a stale lease whose holder is gone.

waitSeconds.description:
While another lease holds the iPhone, retry every second for up to this long
instead of failing with `device-leased`. While it waits, `GET /v1/phones` lists
the client under `waiting`. Cannot be combined with `force`.

expiresAt.description: When the lease ends if no call uses it before. Each call moves it.

replaced.description: The lease that `force` ended, if any

notice.description: A note from ghosthand.dev about the plan, e.g. a failed payment. Show it to the user.

state.description:
`signed-out`: no account on this Mac; every lease fails with `login-required`.
`signing-in`: a browser sign-in runs; open `verificationUrl`. `signed-in`: each
acquire checks the iPhone and this Mac against the plan.

server.description: The ghosthand.dev server the daemon uses (env GHOSTHAND_SERVER at daemon start)

userCode.description: While signing in, the code the browser page shows, to compare

verificationUrl.description: While signing in, the page to open in a browser

lastError.description: Why the last sign-in did not finish (denied or expired), until the next one starts

plan.description:
Only from `GET /v1/account`. `free`: one iPhone, on any Mac. `pro`: every iPhone
on each paid Mac, plus the free iPhone anywhere. Acquire on another iPhone fails
with `subscription-required`.

paidMacs.description: Only from `GET /v1/account`. Macs the Pro subscription pays for; 0 on free

sourceAccess.description: Only from `GET /v1/account`. True when the account can read the daemon source on GitHub

notice.description: Note about the plan to show the user

subscribeUrl.description: Checkout, or the billing portal when subscribed

serverError.description: Only from `GET /v1/account`, when ghosthand.dev could not be reached

address.description: The iPhone's Bluetooth address, read over USB. Its HID link to the Mac uses the same address.

state.description:
`connected`: input works. `disconnected`: paired, the Mac is reconnecting; Bluetooth is off
on the iPhone or it is out of range if this lasts. `notPaired`: pair from iPhone Settings > Bluetooth
(the next input command waits for it).

pointer.description: How taps move the pointer, once known. `absolute` (iOS 17+) goes straight to the spot. `relative` (iOS 15, which ignores absolute positions) pushes the pointer into the top-left corner, then moves it in measured steps

name.description: New name of the iPhone, as in Settings > General > About > Name

RandomKind.description:
`name`, `lastname`: common US first or last name. `username`: lowercase letters and 4
digits, at most 15 chars, also an email username. `birthdate`: YYYY-MM-DD, age 19 to 45.
`password`: 16 chars with uppercase, lowercase, digits and symbols `!@#$%*`, starts uppercase.

reason.description: The lease's task when the value was made

label.description: The lease's label when the value was made

device.description: Screen capture id of the lease's iPhone (the id in `GET /v1/devices`)

deviceName.description: The iPhone's name when the value was made, if it was on USB

width.description: Screenshot width in the request's `scale` space

height.description: Screenshot height in the request's `scale` space

x.description: Left edge, in the request's `scale` space

y.description: Top edge, in the request's `scale` space

x.description: Distance from the left edge, in the request's `scale` space (screen points by default)

y.description: Distance from the top edge, in the request's `scale` space (screen points by default)

TapRequest.description: Either a point (`x` and `y`) or a `text` to find with OCR. Other combinations are rejected.

ScreenFraction.description: A point as fractions of the screen, from the top left corner

x.description: Distance from the left edge, as a fraction of the screen width

y.description: Distance from the top edge, as a fraction of the screen height

TapText.title: Text
TapText.description: Tap the center of an OCR line

text.description: Tap the center of the OCR line that equals or contains this (case-insensitive)

index.description: The nth match, top to bottom (1-based). Needed when several lines match.

durationMs.description: Default is random and human-like, 80-180 ms growing with the distance. It starts fast and lifts while still moving, so feeds keep going. Set it to fix the speed.

HoldRequest.description: Either a point (`x` and `y`) or a `text` to find with OCR, plus an optional `durationMs`.

HoldPoint.title: Point
HoldPoint.description: Hold at a point of the screenshot

x.description: Distance from the left edge, in the request's `scale` space (screen points by default)

y.description: Distance from the top edge, in the request's `scale` space (screen points by default)

HoldText.title: Text
HoldText.description: Hold the center of an OCR line

text.description: Hold the center of the OCR line that equals or contains this (case-insensitive)

index.description: The nth match, top to bottom (1-based). Needed when several lines match.

HoldDuration.description: How long the button stays down without moving

from.description: Where the long press happens and the drag starts

to.description: Where the drag ends and the button is released

durationMs.description: Drag duration after the hold. Slow drags (1000+ ms) let iOS follow the item.

direction.description: `down` shows content further down the page (like swiping a finger up); `right` shows content further right

ticks.description: Number of wheel ticks. See `ghosthand scroll --help` for the distance of one tick.

at.description: Where the pointer scrolls. Default the screen center.

key.description:
A combination like `cmd+space` or `shift+tab` (modifiers `cmd`, `ctrl`, `alt`,
`shift`), a named key (`enter`, `esc`, `backspace`, `tab`, `space`, `up`, `down`,
`left`, `right`, `pageup`, `pagedown`, `end`, `forwarddelete`), `home`, or a media key
(`volumeup`, `volumedown`, `playpause`). For mute use `/mute`.

text.description: US-ASCII text. `\n` presses Enter and `\t` presses Tab.

enter.description: Press Enter after the text (sends a message in Messages)

prompt.description: What to do, in plain words. Without it, `task` must be running and the call follows its turn.

task.description: Id of an earlier task (`Ghosthand-Task`), to continue it with its history
The task id; pass it as `task` to send a follow-up

passcode.description: US-ASCII passcode, digits or alphanumeric. Never logged or stored.

logs.description: Progress lines written while the operation ran

screen.description: The screen text after the input, present when `screentext` was asked

Image.description: The screen after the input, present when `screenshot` was asked

width.description: Image width in the request's `scale` space

height.description: Image height in the request's `scale` space

path.description: Absolute path of a new .mov or .mp4 file on the daemon's Mac. Its folder must exist; the file must not.

fps.description: Frame rate cap, 1 up to the iPhone's rate (usually 60). Default no cap.

maxDurationSeconds.description: Stop by itself after this many seconds, 1...3600.

fps.description: The frame rate cap, if one was asked

audio.description: The recording has a sound track

durationSeconds.description: Time from the first to the last video frame

width.description: Video width in pixels (native screen pixels)

height.description: Video height in pixels (native screen pixels)

droppedFrames.description: Frames the encoder was not ready for. Frames removed by the fps cap are not counted.

audio.description: The file has a sound track

stoppedBy.description:
Why the recording stopped: `request` (record stop), `maxDuration`, `leaseEnded`
(release, idle timeout or `force`), `daemonStopped`, or `disconnected` (the iPhone
left USB).

names.description: File names from `GET photos`, e.g. IMG_0004.PNG

installing.description: Still downloading or installing (an App Store placeholder)

fileSharing.description: Shares its Documents folder; `app` in the files routes reaches it

homeScreen.description: Where its icon is, e.g. `dock`, `page 2`, `page 1, folder Social`. Absent - only in the App Library

SIMInfo.description: SIM state from USB lockdown. A field is absent when the iPhone does not report it (unknown), so never read a missing field as "no SIM". A missing phone number does not mean no SIM either.

telephony.description: The iPhone has a cellular modem (`TelephonyCapability`).

tray.description: Physical SIM tray (`SIMTrayStatus`): `sim` a SIM card is in the tray, `empty` the tray is in without a card, `absent` no tray, `unknown` iOS does not know. An eSIM does not use the tray: check `lines`.

lines.description: Carrier settings of each SIM iOS reads, physical or eSIM (`CarrierBundleInfoArray`). Empty: no SIM is read. A line here does not prove cellular service works (PIN, activation, plan): check Settings > Cellular.

embedded.description: true: eSIM, false: physical SIM card

code.description: Stable error code. Switch on it; `title` and `detail` are for people.

title.description: Short summary of the code, the same for every error with this code

status.description: HTTP status of the error. In stream mode the response status stays 200.

detail.description: What happened and what to do next. Agents should read it.
